summary: Backup Pro is an open-source Flutter Android app that replaces FolderSync for a small group of personal users. It watches chosen phone folders and copies new or changed files to a home NAS over SMB, automatically turning on a VPN first if the phone isn't on the home network, and keeps working in the background with retries if the connection drops.

concepts.title: App screens
concepts.description: The screens someone opens to configure and watch their backups: the home dashboard, NAS settings, and the folder picker.

concepts.title: Premium look & branding
concepts.description: The app's dark navy/blue theme, its cloud-and-arrow logo, and the launch splash screen, kept consistent across every screen.
concepts.notes: The launcher icon is generated by tool/generate_icon.dart (pure vector shapes drawn and rasterized via Flutter's own test-harness renderer) rather than hand-authored artwork, since no image-editing tool was available in this environment.

concepts.title: App version display
concepts.description: Shows the running app's version and build number on the Settings screen, so you can tell which build is installed.

concepts.title: Live transfer dashboard
concepts.description: Shows sync progress, the current file, and simple speed/status stats while a backup is running.

concepts.title: Source/destination folder picker
concepts.description: Lets you pick a phone folder and set exactly where it lands on the NAS, and shows whether each pair has ever synced.
concepts.notes: Each folder card shows Source, Destination and a 'Last synced' / 'Never synced' status. Previously this was clipped out of view by a ListTile sized for fewer lines than it held; rebuilt as a plain card layout so nothing gets cut off.

concepts.title: NAS credentials & connection test
concepts.description: Where you enter the NAS address, share name and login, and a 'Test Connection' button to check it works before saving.

concepts.title: Home screen widget
concepts.description: Native Android home screen widgets, in 3 sizes, showing the latest backup status with a manual 'Backup Now' button.

concepts.title: System notifications
concepts.description: Shows an ongoing notification while syncing and a final one for success, partial failure, or a full failure.

concepts.title: Background scheduler
concepts.description: Runs the backup on its own, without the app open, using Android's WorkManager.
concepts.notes: Was silently broken until this session: BackgroundService().initialize() (which actually sets up WorkManager) was never called anywhere at startup, so every sync attempt threw an uncaught PlatformException. Now wired into main().

concepts.title: Persistent foreground service
concepts.description: Keeps a sticky notification up during an active transfer so Android doesn't kill the app mid-sync.

concepts.title: On-network check
concepts.description: Checks whether the phone can actually reach the NAS right now, before trying to sync.
concepts.notes: Implemented as a raw socket connect to the NAS host/port with a short timeout — no extra plugin needed. Works from both the normal app and Workmanager's separate background process.

concepts.title: VPN auto-connect
concepts.description: If the phone can't reach the NAS directly, launches your chosen VPN app automatically, then re-checks before syncing.
concepts.notes:
Detects which supported VPN app is installed (WireGuard, Tailscale, OpenVPN Connect, NordVPN, ProtonVPN, ExpressVPN, Surfshark) via a native Android check, and you pick your default in Settings.

Major bug fixed this session: scheduled syncs run in WorkManager's own separate background process, which never sees a channel that was only registered on the app's main screen — so the VPN launch silently failed every time a scheduled sync tried to use it. Fixed by launching the VPN app through url_launcher instead, which works in both places.

concepts.title: SMB / CIFS client
concepts.description: Connects to the NAS and uploads files over the SMB protocol, the same one Windows file sharing uses.

concepts.title: One-way archive engine
concepts.description: Compares local files against the last sync time and uploads anything new or changed.
concepts.notes: Strictly one-way archive: files deleted on the phone remain on the NAS. Reads source/destination pairs from folder-pair-config and drives smb-client and network-awareness/vpn-controller before each run.

concepts.title: Retry with backoff
concepts.description: If a connection or upload fails, waits a bit and tries again a few times before giving up on that file, instead of aborting the whole backup.
concepts.notes: File-level retry, not byte-range resume mid-upload (the SMB library used doesn't support append/seek writes cleanly). A folder is only marked fully synced once every file in that pass succeeds, so failures get retried on the next run.

concepts.title: Diagnostic logger
concepts.description: Would capture structured logs of errors and network drops for later debugging.
concepts.notes: Not built yet — sync status is currently just a short string in SharedPreferences plus console prints, no structured/persisted log.

concepts.title: File filter & size limits
concepts.description: Would let you exclude file types or oversized files from a backup.
concepts.notes: Not built yet — folder-scanner currently syncs every modified file with no size or type filtering.

concepts.title: SMS & call log extractor
concepts.description: Would read SMS messages and call history and back them up as JSON.
concepts.notes: Not built yet. Named in the original PRD but no code exists for it.

concepts.title: Folder scanner
concepts.description: Looks through a chosen folder (and its subfolders) for files modified since the last successful sync.
concepts.notes: Requires Android's 'All files access' (MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE) permission to reach beyond standard media folders.

concepts.title: Automated build & GitHub release
concepts.description: Every push to main builds the app, runs its checks, and publishes a versioned, ready-to-install APK as a GitHub Release.
concepts.notes:
Originally intended to push straight to the Google Play Console; that never got built. What exists instead: GitHub Actions builds an AAB (Play Store format, kept for later) and a debug-signed APK, tags a release with the app version + CI run number, and attaches the APK so anyone can download and sideload it.

This pipeline had never once succeeded before this session — flutter analyze treats even style-level notices as fatal by default, and ~19 pre-existing ones meant every single run failed silently from the very first commit. Fixed by scoping the CI gate to real errors/warnings only.

concepts.title: Free / open source license
concepts.description: The repository and app are meant to be distributed under a free open-source license (e.g. MIT or GPLv3).
concepts.notes: Not actually added yet — no LICENSE file exists in the repo.
